items.title: Radar timeline opens on the OLDEST frame, so the Weather screen shows two-hour-stale cloud by default
items.summary: Real and objectively wrong. WeatherScreen held `int _currentFrameIndex = 0` and handed it straight to the scrubber, so first paint sat on frame 1 of N — up to two hours behind the NOW marker the scrubber itself paints at the far right — until the operator dragged or pressed play. Fixed at the cause: the screen now holds `int? _selectedFrameIndex` where null means 'nobody has scrubbed', and the rendered index resolves to `latestObservedRadarFrameIndex(frames)`, a new documented pure helper in radar_timeline_scrubber.dart. It returns the last frame with isForecast false, not simply the last frame, because RainViewer appends nowcast tiles and Open-Meteo / MET Norway append future hours (rainviewer_radar_provider.dart:131-138, openmeteo_cloud_provider.dart:160) — opening on those would show predicted cloud as if it had been measured. All-forecast lists fall back to index 0, the frame nearest to now. Because the state is null until the operator touches the scrubber, the timeline also keeps tracking the live edge across the screen's 5-minute refresh instead of drifting; once they scrub, their choice sticks (still clamped). The finding's second suggestion — repurposing skip-forward to jump to NOW — was NOT done: it is the 'Next frame' step control, and stealing it would remove the only way to step the loop forward.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/weather/weather_screen_opens_on_now_test.dart — two widget tests pump the real WeatherScreen and read the scrubber's own 'Frame N of M' counter (13 observations -> 'Frame 13 of 13'; 10 observations + 3 nowcast -> 'Frame 10 of 13'), plus four unit tests for latestObservedRadarFrameIndex. 6/6 pass; the whole weather set (this file + weather_screen_responsive_test.dart + test/widgets/weather/) is 28/28 green.
items.revert_check: Reverted weather_screen.dart:287 from `(_selectedFrameIndex ?? latestObservedRadarFrameIndex(radarFrames))` back to `(_selectedFrameIndex ?? 0)`: both widget tests failed ('Found 0 widgets with text "Frame 13 of 13"' and '"Frame 10 of 13"'), the four unit tests still passed. Restored, 6/6 green.

items.title: The Slew split-button's primary half does nothing - every slew costs two clicks through a menu
items.summary: Real and objectively wrong. The filled 'Slew' half was a costume: the entire visual child sat inside IgnorePointer with `onPressed: enabled ? () {} : null`, and PopupMenuButton owned the whole hit area, so clicking the word 'Slew' opened a menu whose first entry was also 'Slew'. The commonest action on the control cost two clicks and a menu traversal, and the affordance lied about what the left half did. Fixed at the cause: the widget is now an actual split button — a Row of SkotiqButton (onPressed runs _handleSlewMode(SlewMode.slew) directly) beside a PopupMenuButton carrying only the chevron. Both call sites (mount_tab.dart:431 manual GoTo, framing_actions_panel.dart:316 'Slew to Target') keep their layout; the chevron gained symmetric padding so it is a real tap target instead of a bare 16px glyph. Safety is unchanged: every entry point still runs through _handleSlewMode, so the below-horizon confirm gate, the single-flight latch and the backend-revision guard all still apply — proven by the existing horizon-gate tests, which now drive the primary half. Accessibility: the old wrapper Semantics is gone because SkotiqButton publishes its own button/enabled/label node and is keyboard-focusable; the chevron is wrapped in Semantics(label: 'More slew options') because PopupMenuButton contributes only a 'Show menu' tooltip and would otherwise reach a screen reader unnamed.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/widgets/slew_dropdown_button_test.dart — new 'the primary half slews on ONE click, with no menu' asserts service.calls == 1 after a single tap on the label and that no menu opened; 'the chevron half opens the menu' covers the other half; 'both halves publish a named button node' / 'publishes the disabled state when the mount is down' assert the rendered semantics of both halves. The five horizon-gate tests were rewired to tap the primary half, so the gate is now proven on the one-click path. 11/11 pass. Also re-ran the call-site layout suites: framing (16/16) and mount_tab_coordinates (11/11) green.
items.revert_check: Reverted slew_dropdown_button.dart:133 to the original `onPressed: enabled ? () {} : null`: 6 tests failed, including 'the primary half slews on ONE click, with no menu' and all four horizon-gate dispatch tests. Restored, 11/11 green.

items.title: Pinning a narrator event is invisible on the timeline - the PINNED marker only exists inside the detail sheet
items.summary: Re-verified independently this pass; verdict stands. Not real as filed, on two counts. (1) There is no operator pin anywhere in the product — no toggle in the app, no DAO write, no headless endpoint (narrator_events_dao.dart exposes insert/read only; narrator_handlers.dart:67 serialises `pinned` read-only). `pinned` is set once, by the detector, at emit time (narrator_service.dart:668 <- draft.pinned), so the premise 'pinning exists so an operator can mark the two or three things that mattered' does not hold; the flag is the narrator's own top-of-feed ordering hint. (2) Every production emitter that sets pinned: true also sets category: discovery AND severity: celebrate — discovery_detectors.dart:47-59, :188-205, :238-253 and first_light_detectors.dart:62-78, :117-135 are the complete set. The timeline already renders exactly that combination distinctly: _TimelineRow computes `isDiscovery` from discovery-or-celebrate and gives the rail a 16px node with the sparkles glyph instead of a 10px dot (night_story_timeline.dart:593, 645-689), and NarratorCard paints the celebrate accent->primary gradient edge that no other severity gets (narrator_card.dart:90-103). So an app-produced pinned row is never 'visually identical to the two unpinned rows'; the repro reached that state by hand-setting pinned=1 in the DB on an event the app would never pin. A pin glyph would restate what the sparkles node and gradient edge already say, and a 'Pinned only' chip would duplicate the existing Discoveries chip (pinned is a strict subset of discovery). Residual worth the owner's eye, deliberately NOT changed here: the detail sheet's 'PINNED' chip (narrator_detail_sheet.dart:86-93) names an internal ordering flag the operator can neither set nor clear, which is a copy/product call rather than a defect to fix silently.

items.title: The narrator detail sheet shows a 'PINNED' badge for a flag no operator can set or clear
items.summary: Surfaced while confirming the 'not-real' verdict above, and deliberately left for the owner. `pinned` is an internal ordering hint written only by the discovery/first-light detectors; the DAO exposes insertEvent plus reads and nothing else, and /api/narrator/feed serialises the field read-only. But narrator_detail_sheet.dart:86-93 prints the word 'PINNED' to the operator. Reading 'PINNED' on a card, an astrophotographer will look for the pin control — NINA's and SGP's equivalents are all operator-set — and there is none to find. The label is real product surface for a flag that is not a product feature. This is a product call, not a defect: it turns on whether the owner wants operator pinning to exist, so I did not implement anything.
items.options: (a) Leave the badge as-is: it does explain why a discovery sits at the top of the feed, and costs nothing to ship. (b) Retitle it to something purely descriptive — 'HIGHLIGHT', 'TOP MOMENT' — so it reads as the narrator's own emphasis rather than an action the operator has taken or can undo; pure copy change, no schema or DAO work. (c) Make pinning real: add an updatePinned write to narrator_events_dao.dart, a pin toggle in the detail sheet, a headless PATCH, and a 'Pinned only' filter chip on the NIGHT STORY timeline — genuinely useful over an eight-hour night, but it is a new feature with schema-adjacent write paths and sync implications for the hub, not a polish item.
items.recommendation: (b) now, and treat (c) as a separate feature the owner decides on its own merits. (b) removes the false affordance for the cost of one string while keeping the useful signal that the narrator considered this event a headline. (a) leaves the app implying a control it does not have, which is the same cry-wolf shape this campaign has been closing elsewhere; (c) is real value but should not be smuggled in under a P3 widget finding.
